thread:
evan: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel routing tweak I see p99 tail spikes on short-chat workloads. spike looks correlated with fallback->slow-kernel path + kv cache churn. attaching quick numbers.

linh: Can you paste the profiler snippet and microbatch stats?

ev an: putting the key bits below. noticed p95 okay but p99 doubled for requests < 50 tokens. kv_cache_miss_rate jumped from 6% to 18% in canary region. microbatch size distribution shifted right (mode 6 -> 10).

priya: yikes. do we know if it’s batching or kernel latency on fallback?

ev an: both. kernel fallback latency median is fine but variance huge when batch >8. combined with kv cache misses we see tail amplification. snippet: 
```
p95_latency_ms: 180 -> 210
p99_latency_ms: 420 -> 1200
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.06 -> 0.18
microbatch_size_mode: 6 -> 10
slow_kernel_p99_ms: 600 -> 1600
```

nathan: Any recent change to truncation or max_tokens caps? those protect tails historically.

ev an: earlier change removed a hard max_tokens cap for RLHF jobs to allow longer completions. that exposed hot-paths where long requests push kernel choice into fallback due to memory pressure.

linh: Proposal: reintroduce conservative per-route max_tokens caps (soft cap + adaptive truncation), add fast-path kernel preference for small requests, and a prefetch/kv-priming tweak to reduce misses. rough config: 
```
runtime.tail_protection:
  per_route_max_tokens_cap: 512  # soft cap, configurable per model/route
  truncation_strategy: right_trim_prefix_weighted
  microbatch_limit: 6
  kernel_preference: [attn_opt_fast, fallback_last]
  kv_prefetch_window: 2  # prefetch next 2 token blocks for streaming
```

priya: I like soft caps (don't return error, just truncate + signal). can we also add a fast-path that bypasses batching for tiny requests (<32 tokens) to cut tail amplification?

ev an: yes — microbatch bypass for tiny requests already exists but was relaxed. suggest re-enable strict bypass threshold at 32 and block microbatching in mixed-size batches (don't let tiny requests wait behind large ones).

nathan: How to roll this safely? metrics to watch: p95/p99, kv_cache_miss, CPU/GPU mem pressure, error rate, token truncation rate. also watch quality regression via eval set.

linh: Plan: implement soft cap + truncation logic server-side (fast path), tweak kernel preference heuristic (prefer fast kernel for seq_len<=128), set microbatch_limit to 6, re-enable tiny-request bypass. Canary in us-west-2 on 10% hosts for 2 hours then 30% for 4 hours.

priya: Add telemetry: emit truncated=true + truncation_reason tags and model/kernel chosen. add alert when truncation_rate > 1% for a route.

nathan: Also add p99_delta rollout gate: if p99 improves or stays same within 10% and errors unchanged, proceed. else auto-rollback.

ops-bot: deploy job queued: deploy/runtime/tail-protection-canary -> queued by linh. ETA ~25m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

priya: quick note — for KV prefetch we must avoid extra memory thrash. prefetch window=2 seems safe, but let's cap total prefetched bytes per worker.

evan: agreed. I'll open a PR with the config + tests and a small microbench harness to measure kernel_choice distribution and kv misses. assigning to lin h for rollout.

linh: will take it. thumbs if you agree with the plan. :thumbsup: :eyes:

nathan: +1. schedule post-mortem if rollback triggered.

sre-oncall: I'll add dashboard panels and a temporary alert for kv_cache_miss_rate > 12% on canary hosts.

evan: thanks everyone. PR link once ready — will include the small profiling script and expected thresholds to validate canary.

priya: one more thought — for models that are extremely bursty, consider an adaptive truncation weight that preserves prefix tokens with higher probability to keep responses meaningful. we can iterate after first canary.

linh: noted. capturing that as follow-up.

ops-bot: deploy/runtime/tail-protection-canary started on 10 hosts (us-west-2).
